subject: extreme lod scores during ehk regression

messages.author: 130b82f78232556c
messages.subject: extreme lod scores during ehk regression
parts:
Dear Karl Broman and group members,

I'm working on an F2 mapping population with selective genotyping (~500 phenotypes with ~50 genotypes from the extremes) and outbred grandparents. I am using the 4way cross genotype notation, including individuals without genoytpes in the analysis, and using a covariate (cytoplasm type) which is well balanced among the extreme phenotypes.

For the most part, the data are behaving relatively well during single QTL analysis. Most of the mapping approaches I have tried (marker regression, standard interval mapping, Haley-Knott regression, multiple imputation) give reasonable and roughly similar patterns of lod scores across the chromosomes. However, when I use extended Haley-Knott regression, I get very strange output in which most markers have a lod score of 400 and some have very small lod scores (400 looks a ceiling). Note that I also get the warning "X'X matrix is singular" during this analysis but not the others (I checked for monomorphic markers but that doesn't appear to be the problem).

Is it possible that the ehk regression is incompatible with the 4way cross notation?

Any insight would be greatly appreciated!
Thanks,
Kate

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] extreme lod scores during ehk regression
parts:
The extended Haley-Knott method has a tendency to misbehave. Since you're getting good results by other methods, I would just stick with those and ignore method="eh".

Regards,
karl
